fig.S1: Quality control across the five co-integrated cohorts. (A) Detected genes per cell, by cohort; dashed lines are the retention window of 300 to 8,000 genes. (B) Percentage of reads mapping to mitochondrial genes, by cohort; dashed line is the 20% cut-off. Boxes are the interquartile range with the median, whiskers 1.5 times the interquartile range, outliers omitted. (C) Cells retained after quality control in each of the 63 samples, ordered by yield on a logarithmic scale and coloured by cohort. GSE291389 is single-nucleus and therefore has near-zero mitochondrial content and the highest gene counts; GSE203191 is the shallowest library.
fig.S2: Marker evidence for the ten immune states (110,035 immune cells). Colour is mean expression of each gene standardised across states, dot size the fraction of cells in the state expressing the gene, and vertical rules separate the marker group belonging to each state. Cell numbers per state are given in parentheses. Each state expresses its own canonical markers and little of the others', with the expected exceptions that Treg cells share the pan-T markers and plasmacytoid dendritic cells share plasma-cell transcripts.
fig.S3: The same calibration failure across 124 diseases (6,111 cell-type comparisons in 523 public case–control settings from the CZ CELLxGENE Census; none gynaecological, none sharing a dataset with this study). (A) False-positive rate of the two tests when the disease label is permuted across donors 1,000 times per setting; violins with the interquartile range and median marked, dashed line at the nominal 0.05 and the medians printed above. (B) Median false-positive rate against the number of donors in the study; the pooled-cell test remains far above nominal at every cohort size. (C) Fraction of comparisons called significant by each test on the observed labels, with the share of pooled-significant results that are not upheld at the donor level.
fig.S4: Transcriptional menstrual-cycle phase. (A) Phase score in the ten samples whose GEO record reports a cycle phase; the score separates them with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.88 (five proliferative, five secretory; one-sided Mann–Whitney P = 0.028). (B) Phase score by disease status in the two cohorts containing controls; the groups do not differ (P = 0.88), so cycle phase does not explain the patient-level null. Bars are medians.
fig.S5: Patient-level composition of all ten immune states. (A) Share of immune cells in each state, one point per patient, on a symmetric-logarithmic axis with medians marked (7 control and 34 endometriosis patients from the three cohorts containing controls). (B) Combined evidence for a difference in each state, as $-$log$_{10}$ of the P value from Stouffer combination across cohorts, with the Benjamini–Hochberg q value printed; the dashed line marks P = 0.05. Macrophages and mast cells are the nearest misses and neither survives correction.
fig.S6: Sensitivity of the spatial macrophage finding. (A) Leaving out each patient in turn; every four-patient subset still has all four patients up, and with four pairs the smallest attainable one-sided P value is 0.062, so these are the strongest values the design allows. (B) Leaving out each of the nine composite genes in turn. (C) The composite compared with three alternative marker sets, with the number of genes measured and the number shared with the composite; the focal scavenger-receptor and complement module and the WikiPathways macrophage set both separate lesion from eutopic tissue, while a broad published M2 signature does not. Dotted lines mark the full five-patient estimate; points are filled when P < 0.05.
fig.S7: Kaplan–Meier survival curves for the malignant epithelial signature. (A) GSE65986, clear-cell and endometrioid ovarian carcinoma with progression-free survival (55 patients, 15 events). (B) TCGA-OV, predominantly high-grade serous carcinoma with overall survival (428 patients, 265 events). Patients are split at the median signature score; log-rank and Cox P values are given in each panel and numbers at risk beneath.
fig.S8: The cross-disease calibration result broken down by tissue and by disease. (A) False-positive rate of the pooled-cell test in each tissue with at least 150 comparisons; all eight lie between 0.77 and 0.88 against a nominal 0.05, with the number of comparisons at the right. (B) Percentage of pooled-significant results not upheld at donor level; seven of the eight tissues exceed 60%, the exception being large intestine at 29%. (C) The same false-positive rate for each disease with at least 100 comparisons; eleven of twelve lie between 0.81 and 0.88 and dementia is the single exception at 0.10.
fig.S9: Composition of the atlas across all eight lineages. (A) Share of cells assigned to each lineage in every tissue with at least 500 cells, with the cell count in thousands and the number of samples at the right. Endometrium combines two spellings of the same tissue label in the source metadata and is therefore one row, not two. The two organoid libraries are epithelium by protocol and the clear-cell carcinoma libraries are single-nucleus. (B) The same composition by cohort, which is why cohort enters every model as a covariate.
fig.S10: Design and technical behaviour of the segmented spatial cohort (GSE263897). (A) Number of profiled regions contributed by each patient, for every combination of segment type and tissue; the design is balanced, with two regions in every combination. (B) Number of genes detected above the array mean in each region, by segment type and tissue, with medians marked; macrophage segments carry less signal than stromal or epithelial segments, but lesion and eutopic regions of the same segment type are comparable. (C) Agreement between the two replicate regions of the same patient in the nine-gene composite, coloured by segment type, with the identity line dashed.

tab.S1: Per-sample immune composition for all 81 samples. Immune-state percentages and programme scores are given for the 41 samples of the two cohorts carried into the ten-state scan; the 40 samples of GSE213216 contribute Treg fractions and immune-cell yields only. Columns: gsm, GEO sample accession; dataset, cohort accession; cond, Control or Endometriosis; n_immune, immune cells recovered; Treg_pct and the ten pct_<state> columns (pct_B, pct_CD4T, pct_CD8T, pct_Macrophage, pct_Mast, pct_Mono, pct_NK, pct_Plasma, pct_Treg, pct_pDC), percentage of that sample's immune cells in the state; log_Treg_pct, log(Treg_pct + 0.1), the response used in the stratified model; M2_in_mac, CD8_exh and NK_cyt, mean programme scores in macrophages, CD8 T cells and NK cells. The table is set in parts that repeat the sample identifiers, so a reader can line the parts up sample by sample. Treg_pct and pct_Treg are the same quantity: Treg_pct is available for all 81 samples and pct_Treg only for the 41 with the full ten-state breakdown.
tab.S2: Patient-level paired spatial results for all three segment types. Columns: n_patients, patients contributing paired regions; eutopic_mean and lesion_mean, mean composite score for that tissue after averaging a patient's replicate regions; mean_diff, lesion minus eutopic; n_pat_up, patients higher in lesion; p_paired_1sided, one-sided paired Wilcoxon signed-rank P value.
tab.S3: scIB integration benchmark metrics. Columns: Embedding, the representation tested; the remainder are the scib-metrics outputs under their package names. Bio-conservation metrics: Isolated labels, KMeans NMI, KMeans ARI, Silhouette label, cLISI. Batch-correction metrics: BRAS (batch-removal-adapted silhouette), iLISI, KBET, Graph connectivity, PCR comparison. Bio conservation and Batch correction are the means of their five metrics and Total is 0.6 x Bio conservation + 0.4 x Batch correction, all verified against the values in the sheet; every metric runs 0 to 1 with higher better. A Metric Type entry accompanies each metric and labels its group; it is not data. The sheet holds the embeddings as rows and the metrics as columns, and the table is set transposed here so the metric names read down the page.
tab.S4: Sensitivity analyses of the spatial macrophage finding: leave-one-patient-out, leave-one-gene-out, per-gene tests, and three external gene sets (published M2 signature, WikiPathways macrophage markers, ad hoc disjoint alternative-activation markers). Columns: analysis, which of the four analyses the row belongs to; patient_left_out, gene_removed and gene, the item excluded or tested; n, pairs remaining; up, patients higher in lesion; mean_diff and diff, lesion minus eutopic composite; P, one-sided paired Wilcoxon; set, the marker set a gene belongs to; gene_set and source, the external set and its origin; n_genes_measured and overlap_with_composite, genes of that set present in the data and shared with the nine-gene composite; macrophage_up, stroma_up and epithelium_up, patients higher in lesion out of five, and macrophage_diff, stroma_diff and epithelium_diff with macrophage_P, stroma_P and epithelium_P, the mean difference and one-sided paired Wilcoxon P of the same test within each segment type.
tab.S5: Patient-level composition scan across all ten immune states, per cohort and combined, with Benjamini–Hochberg q values. Columns: immune_state; P_GSE179640 and P_GSE214411, one-sided Mann-Whitney p per cohort; z_combined and P_combined, Stouffer combination across cohorts; q_combined_BH, Benjamini–Hochberg q across the ten states.
tab.S6: Power and minimum detectable effect for the patient-level Treg comparison, per cohort and combined. Columns: n_ctrl and n_case, samples per group; pooled_ctrl_pct and pooled_case_pct, Treg percentage when that cohort's cells are pooled; pooled_implied_delta, the difference pooling implies; between_sample_SD, standard deviation of the per-sample percentages; MDE_80pct_power, smallest difference detectable at 80% power; power_for_pooled_delta, power for the pooled-implied difference; controls_needed_80pct, control donors that would give 80% power; power_combined_81samples, power of the combined dataset-stratified test over all 81 samples.
tab.S7: Cell-type composition tested with propeller and scCODA on the same donor-by-cell-type counts. Columns: tool and dataset, the test and the cohort; the remainder follow each tool's own output. propeller: CellType, PropMean.Control and PropMean.Endometriosis (group mean proportions), Tstatistic, P.Value, FDR (Benjamini–Hochberg). scCODA: Cell Type, Final Parameter and log2-fold change (the selected effect, zero on every row here because the credible set is empty), Inclusion probability (posterior probability that the state is included).
tab.S8: Transcriptional menstrual-cycle phase score per sample, its validation against reported phase, and the phase-adjusted model. Columns: gsm, GEO sample accession; dataset, cohort accession; condition, Control or Endometriosis; reported_phase, the cycle phase recorded in the GEO metadata where one was given; phase_score, mean z-scored secretory minus proliferative marker expression.
